title: Was Christmas better in the past?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: a feeling of happiness and also some sadness when you think about a thing that happened in the past
seeing only the positive parts of something and not the negative

sentences.en: Hello and welcome to 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听 BBC Learning English 的 6 Minute English。

sentences.en: I’m Beth. And I’m Neil. Now, it’s Christmas time in the UK at the moment.
sentences.zh: 我是 Beth。我是 Neil。现在，英国正值圣诞时节。

sentences.en: And like with celebrations around the world, lots of people have many happy memories about Christmas.
sentences.zh: 就像世界各地的庆祝活动一样，很多人对圣诞节都有许多美好的回忆。

sentences.en: Beth, do you have any happy Christmas memories?
sentences.zh: Beth，你有什么快乐的圣诞回忆吗？

sentences.en: I have a lot. Um, my cousins and I used to always put on a Christmas performance for the family.
sentences.zh: 我有很多。嗯，我和我的表亲们以前总是为全家人准备一场圣诞表演。

sentences.en: That was always fun. What about you? Christmas was magical.
sentences.zh: 那总是很有趣。你呢？圣诞节曾经很神奇。

sentences.en: I lived in Canada when I was a kid and it was always snowing, so it just felt perfect.
sentences.zh: 我小时候住在加拿大，那里总是下雪，所以感觉非常完美。

sentences.en: Amazing. Well, at this time of year, we might look back at the Christmases from the past, from our childhood, and feel like they were happier or more magical than Christmas feels today.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。在这个时节，我们可能会回首过去的圣诞节，回首童年，觉得那时的圣诞节比现在的更快乐、更神奇。

sentences.en: Yes, thinking about the past can make us feel happy and sad at the same time.
sentences.zh: 是的，回想过去会让我们同时感到快乐和忧伤。

sentences.en: It’s a strange feeling we call nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 这是一种奇怪的感觉，我们称之为“怀旧”（nostalgia）。

sentences.en: And we’re going to be talking about nostalgia today as well as Christmas memories and traditions.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要聊聊怀旧，还有圣诞回忆和传统。

sentences.en: And as usual, we’ll be learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 像往常一样，我们将学习一些有用的新单词和短语。

sentences.en: You can practise these with the quiz and the worksheet on our website.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过我们网站上的测试和工作单来练习这些内容。

sentences.en: Go to bbclearningenglish.com. First, Beth, I have a question for you.
sentences.zh: 请访问 bbclearningenglish.com。首先，Beth，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: In the UK, the most popular Christmas meal is a roast turkey.
sentences.zh: 在英国，最受欢迎的圣诞大餐是烤火鸡。

sentences.en: Ooh yes, and all the roast potatoes and Brussels sprouts.
sentences.zh: 哦是的，还有所有的烤土豆和抱子甘蓝。

sentences.en: That’s right, yes. But which of these has become a popular food to eat at Christmas time in Japan?
sentences.zh: 没错。但在日本，以下哪种食物已成为圣诞节期间流行的食品？

sentences.en: a) turkey ramen b) fried chicken c) takeaway pizza I think the answer is fried chicken.
sentences.zh: a) 火鸡拉面 b) 炸鸡 c) 外卖披萨。我想答案是炸鸡。

sentences.en: Well, we’ll find out at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们将在节目最后揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Now, at Christmas people often create family traditions that they repeat every year.
sentences.zh: 现在，在圣诞节，人们经常会创立每年重复的家庭传统。

sentences.en: Common traditions in the UK including putting out a snack for Father Christmas, that’s Santa Claus, who delivers presents for children.
sentences.zh: 英国常见的传统包括为圣诞老人（Father Christmas，即 Santa Claus）准备一份零食，他负责给孩子们送礼物。

sentences.en: Well, here is host of BBC Radio 4’s All in the Mind, Claudia Hammond, talking to psychology professor Daryl O’Connor about his Christmas traditions.
sentences.zh: 好的，下面是 BBC Radio 4 节目 All in the Mind 的主持人 Claudia Hammond 与心理学教授 Daryl O’Connor 讨论他的圣诞传统。

sentences.en: Hello Daryl, I wonder whether you think nostalgia for Christmas past influences your Christmas present plans?
sentences.zh: 你好 Daryl，我想知道你是否认为对过去圣诞节的怀旧会影响你现在的圣诞计划？

sentences.en: Daryl O’Connor Well, indeed it does, Claudia.
sentences.zh: Daryl O’Connor：确实如此，Claudia。

sentences.en: So, actually, I look back on my childhood Christmases with lots and lots of nostalgia.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上，我带着满满的怀旧之情回首童年时代的圣诞节。

sentences.en: So, when I was a child, every single Christmas morning we would have to queue up on the stairs, and my father would go in the front room of the house, just to double check, just in case Santa Claus was still there, and then we had to wait.
sentences.zh: 我小时候，每个圣诞节早晨我们都得在楼梯上排队，我父亲会进到屋子的前厅去再次确认，以防圣诞老人还在那里，然后我们必须等待。

sentences.en: And then of course, I have repeated that exact same thing for my children.
sentences.zh: 然后当然，我也对我的孩子们重复了完全相同的事情。

sentences.en: They line up on the stairs as well? How sweet.
sentences.zh: 他们也在楼梯上排队吗？真温馨。

sentences.en: Dying for their presents! When Claudia asks Daryl whether nostalgia influences his present-day Christmases, Daryl responds, indeed it does.
sentences.zh: 渴望得到他们的礼物！当 Claudia 问 Daryl 怀旧是否影响他现在的圣诞节时，Daryl 回答说，“确实如此”（indeed it does）。

sentences.en: This is a common conversational way to say yes, or agree with someone, we say indeed, followed by do in the present tense.
sentences.zh: 这是一种常见的口语表达方式，用于表示肯定或同意某人的观点，我们会说 indeed，后面跟着现在时态的 do。

sentences.en: On Christmas morning, Daryl asks his children to queue up on the stairs so he can check for Santa Claus, just like Daryl’s father did when he was small.
sentences.zh: 在圣诞节早晨，Daryl 让他的孩子们在楼梯上排队，以便他检查圣诞老人是否在，就像 Daryl 小时候他父亲所做的那样。

sentences.en: And Claudia likes this tradition, imagining the children waiting on the stairs, dying for their presents.
sentences.zh: Claudia 很喜欢这个传统，想象着孩子们在楼梯上等待，渴望得到他们的礼物。

sentences.en: We use the phrase dying for informally when someone really wants something.
sentences.zh: 我们在非正式场合使用 dying for 这个短语，表示某人非常想要某样东西。

sentences.en: Now, when we remember Christmas from the past and feel nostalgia, we often remember things in a very positive way.
sentences.zh: 现在，当我们回忆过去的圣诞节并感到怀旧时，我们通常会以非常积极的方式记住事情。

sentences.en: But was the past definitely better? Are we remembering correctly?
sentences.zh: 但过去真的更好吗？我们的记忆准确吗？

sentences.en: This is what Claudia Hammond asked Catherine Loveday, who's a professor of cognitive neuroscience, on BBC Radio 4 programme, All in the Mind.
sentences.zh: 这是 Claudia Hammond 在 BBC Radio 4 节目 All in the Mind 中询问认知神经科学教授 Catherine Loveday 的问题。

sentences.en: How accurate are nostalgic memories? Are they accurate?
sentences.zh: 怀旧的记忆有多准确？它们准确吗？

sentences.en: Well, they’re often going to be rose-tinted and made more positive of course, and that’s what we do with our past generally, but it doesn’t really matter.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们通常会被加上“玫瑰色滤镜”（rose-tinted），当然也会变得更积极，这通常就是我们对待过去的方式，但这其实并不重要。

sentences.en: I mean, in our work we’ve just shown that the function of memory is not about accuracy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在我们的研究中，我们刚刚证明了记忆的功能不在于准确性。

sentences.en: It doesn’t matter if some of the details are wrong, it doesn’t matter how we frame it.
sentences.zh: 即使有些细节是错误的也没关系，我们如何构建（frame）它也没关系。

sentences.en: In fact, it’s actually better for us in a way to reframe our memories and to slightly adjust them to suit who we are now.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在某种程度上，重新构建我们的记忆并稍微调整它们以适应现在的自己，对我们反而更好。

sentences.en: Catherine says that our memories are often rose-tinted.
sentences.zh: Catherine 说我们的记忆通常是“带玫瑰色的”（rose-tinted）。

sentences.en: If a memory is rose-tinted, we only see the positive things about it, and don’t remember any of the bad parts.
sentences.zh: 如果一段记忆是 rose-tinted，我们只看到其中积极的一面，而记不住任何不好的部分。

sentences.en: But, according to Catherine, it doesn’t always matter.
sentences.zh: 但是，根据 Catherine 的说法，这并不总是很重要。

sentences.en: She says the function of memory is not accuracy.
sentences.zh: 她说记忆的功能（function）不是准确性。

sentences.en: Function means the purpose of something.
sentences.zh: Function 的意思是某事物的目的。

sentences.en: In fact, Catherine says that how we frame a memory doesn’t matter.
sentences.zh: 事实上，Catherine 说我们如何构建（frame）一段记忆并不重要。

sentences.en: Frame can be used as a verb to mean how we think of or describe something, like a memory.
sentences.zh: Frame 可以用作动词，意思是我们要如何思考或描述某事，比如一段记忆。

sentences.en: So, our memories aren’t that accurate, and it isn’t that important, unless of course, we need to remember factual details about something important.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的记忆并没有那么准确，这也没那么重要，当然，除非我们需要记住关于某些重要事情的事实细节。

sentences.en: So, our nostalgia about Christmas memories might not be based on what things were actually like in the past, but we shouldn’t worry too much!
sentences.zh: 所以，我们对圣诞回忆的怀旧可能并非基于过去真实的样貌，但我们不必太担心！

sentences.en: And I think it’s time I revealed the answer to my quiz question, Beth.
sentences.zh: 我想是时候揭晓我的测验答案了，Beth。

sentences.en: I asked what has become a traditional food to eat in Japan at Christmas time?
sentences.zh: 我问的是，在日本，什么已经成为了圣诞节的传统食物？

sentences.en: And I said fried chicken, was I right? You are absolutely correct.
sentences.zh: 我说是炸鸡，我对了吗？你完全正确。

sentences.en: Let’s recap the vocabulary we’ve learnt, starting with nostalgia, a feeling of happiness and also some sadness when you think about a thing that happened in the past.
sentences.zh: 让我们回顾一下学过的词汇，首先是 nostalgia（怀旧），当你想到过去发生的事情时，一种既感到快乐又有些忧伤的感觉。

sentences.en: The phrase indeed followed by the present simple form of do can be used informally instead of answering yes.
sentences.zh: 短语 indeed 后面跟着 do 的一般现在时形式，可以非正式地用于代替回答 yes。

sentences.en: For example, Beth, do you enjoy eating Brussels sprouts at Christmas?
sentences.zh: 例如，Beth，你喜欢在圣诞节吃抱子甘蓝吗？

sentences.en: Indeed, I do! Dying for something is an informal phrasal verb we use to say that we really want something.
sentences.zh: 确实喜欢！Dying for something 是一个非正式的短语动词，我们用它来表示非常想要某样东西。

sentences.en: Rose-tinted means seeing only the positive parts of something, and not the bad parts.
sentences.zh: Rose-tinted 的意思是只看到事物积极的部分，而看不到不好的部分。

sentences.en: Function means the purpose of something.
sentences.zh: Function 的意思是某事物的目的。

sentences.en: And frame can be used as a verb to mean how we think of or describe something.
sentences.zh: Frame 可以用作动词，意思是我们要如何思考或描述某事。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. Test what you’ve learnt in the episode with the quiz and worksheet on our website.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟时间又到了。通过我们网站上的测试和工作单来检测你在本集节目中学到的内容。

sentences.en: To all our listeners who are celebrating Christmas, Merry Christmas!
sentences.zh: 祝所有庆祝圣诞节的听众们，圣诞快乐！

sentences.en: And we hope you all have a good end to the year.
sentences.zh: 我们希望大家都能度过一个美好的岁末。

sentences.en: See you soon. Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。拜拜。
